effect_estimate.comment: Purely qualitative and descriptive assessment with no inferential statistical effect estimate; exact descriptive counts and adaptation cost calculations reported in the text are summarized.
effect_estimate.value: Qualitative — no numeric effect estimate reported. Despite inclusive national water, sanitation, and disability policies, Malawi's Disability Act (2012) does not make institutional inclusive WASH legally binding, and national standards, monitoring, budgeting, and enforcement are absent. Across all 10 primary schools (7 public, 3 private), 0 of 10 fully met WHO disability-friendly WASH standards (only 1 public school had a dedicated disability-sensitive latrine; 0 of 10 had water access ramps, handrails, or latrine doors >=1 m wide). Among 23 interviewed students with disabilities, 11/23 reported water access barriers and 13/23 reported sanitation barriers (with 10/23 reducing food and liquid intake to avoid school latrines). Teachers and officials had never proactively consulted students with disabilities, and school hierarchies hindered trained special education teachers from implementing changes. Adapting existing school sanitation facilities to WHO standards using local materials cost MK 28,000 to MK 74,600 (median/average MK 54,000 [USD $78]).

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 by qualitative study design (CASP Qualitative Checklist). Rated 2 because the authors directly observed school WASH infrastructure and interviewed disabled students, teachers, and district officials to document how non-binding statutory provisions, absent monitoring/funding, lack of student consultation, and school hierarchies impede inclusive WASH implementation.

mechanism_flags.comment: Examines disability-inclusive WASH accommodations and low-cost facility adaptations (DISCRETION_ACCOMMODATION, accommodation), lack of proactive consultation with disabled students and School Management Committee roles (participation), headmaster/school-owner gatekeeping over special needs teachers' proposals (discretion), non-binding status of the Disability Act 2012 and absence of national standards, monitoring, and accountability/enforcement (ENFORCEMENT), and annual parental O&M fees of MK 500 plus unfunded school adaptation costs (BURDEN, fees).

study_design.value: Qualitative assessment combining structured field observations (WHO WASH standards checklist), interviews with students, teachers, and government officials, and descriptive local market adaptation cost calculations
